# Model and source

Hasegawa and Duffull (2018) reduced the 28-state calcium-homeostasis and
bone-remodelling model of Peterson and Riggs to eight nonlinear states by
inductive linearization followed by automated proper lumping, then fitted the
reduced model, and two empirical comparators, to the first 12 months of mean
lumbar spine BMD data after denosumab and used all three to predict the
following 36 months. The paper contributes three model files:

| Model file | Structure |
|---|---|
| `Hasegawa_2018_denosumab_qsp` | Reduced eight-state bone-biology QSP model (Eqs 21-28 and 4) |
| `Hasegawa_2018_denosumab_bmd_direct` | Empirical direct response with time-varying Emax (Eq 11) |
| `Hasegawa_2018_denosumab_bmd_turnover` | Empirical turnover model with Imax inhibition of BMD loss (Eq 12) |

All three share the same fixed two-compartment quasi-steady-state TMDD model of
subcutaneous denosumab (Sutjandra 2011, as coded by the authors; Appendix S1).

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Hasegawa_2018_denosumab_qsp"))$reference`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1002/psp4.12324>
* Open-access full text: <https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC6157701/>

```{r load-models}
nms <- c(
  qsp = "Hasegawa_2018_denosumab_qsp",
  direct = "Hasegawa_2018_denosumab_bmd_direct",
  turnover = "Hasegawa_2018_denosumab_bmd_turnover"
)
uis <- lapply(nms, function(n) rxode2::rxode(readModelDb(n)))
```

# Population

The models were fitted to arm-mean lumbar spine BMD (percent change from
baseline) digitized by the authors from the phase 2 dose-ranging study of
denosumab in postmenopausal women with low bone mineral density (McClung 2006,
48-month extension reported by Miller 2008). The every-6-month arms used for
estimation enrolled 54, 47, 42 and 47 women at 14, 60, 100 and 210 mg
(Hasegawa 2018 Results). Only months 0-12 entered the fits; the 60 mg arm over
months 12-48 was the extrapolation test. The digitized data are Table S2 of the
paper. Because the data are arm means, the models are typical-value models with
an additive residual error and no between-subject variability.

```{r population}
str(uis$qsp$population)
```

# Source trace

The authors published their NONMEM control stream for the final nonlinear
lumped model (Appendix S3, `nonlinear_lumped.mod`) and their MATLAB lumping
code (Appendix S2). The stream is the as-run implementation and is followed
wherever it is more precise than the printed Table 1. The stream works in
30-day months (every per-hour rate is multiplied by 24 x 30); the packaged models
work in hours with the same values, and one "month" in this article is 720 h.

| Element | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Reduced model ODEs | Eqs 21-28 | Paper Results; stream `$DES` |
| BMD indirect response | Eq 4, R_in = k_out x 100 | Paper Methods; stream `RIN_BMD`, `K_BMD` |
| Initial conditions | L1 30,082; L2 1.4001; CMX 2.2283e-4; OC 0.0012; TGF 0.2281; ROB 0.0010; FOB 0.0040; SOB 0.0010 | Eqs 13-20; stream `IC1`-`IC8` |
| Fixed bone rate constants | Table 1 "before estimation" | Table 1; stream `$THETA` |
| `ld_oc` | 0.0898 /h | Table 1, after estimation (5.4% RSE) |
| `lr_lumped2` | 0.00337 /h | Table 1, after estimation (9.1% RSE) |
| `lkss_rankl` | 63.4 ng/mL | Table 1, after estimation (63.7% RSE) |
| `lkout` (QSP) | 0.000533 /h | Results text (24.6% RSE) |
| `gam_ob_bmd`, `gam_oc_bmd` | 0.0739, 0.0779 | Stream `$THETA` 19-20 (FIX); not printed in the paper |
| Hill constants (rho, a, delta, gamma) | see derivation check below | Stream `$PK` derivations; Table 1 |
| Denosumab CL, V1, Q, V2, ka, F | 3.06 mL/h, 2.49 L, 37.9 mL/h, 1.36 L, 0.212 /day x (66/71.5)^-0.577, 0.638 | Stream `$THETA` 22-27 |
| `lkint` | 0.00795 /h | Table 1; stream `$DES` |
| `lkss` (PK) | 1380 ng/mL | MATLAB `Model_parameter_values0.m` (`Kss = 138*10`); see below |
| `lrbase_target`, `lkdeg` | 614 ng/mL, 0.00148 /h | MATLAB `Model_parameter_values0.m` |
| Direct model Emax, T1/2, C50 | 5.92 %, 3.12 months, 2.05 ng/mL | Table 2 |
| Turnover model Imax, k_out, C50 | 0.0577, 0.000336 /h, 52.5 ng/mL | Table 2 |
| Residual variances | 0.382, 0.328, 0.387 (%BMD)^2 | Tables 1 and 2; `addSd` is the square root |

## Derived constants against Table 1

The stream parameterizes each Hill function by its baseline fraction and span
and derives the half-maximal driver so the reduced model reproduces the original
model's values at `t0`. Recomputing those derivations reproduces the rounded
Table 1 entries.

```{r derived-constants}
ini_val <- function(ui, nm) ui$iniDf$est[ui$iniDf$name == nm]
q <- uis$qsp
tgf0 <- ini_val(q, "tgfb_act0")
oc0 <- ini_val(q, "oc0")
pil0 <- ini_val(q, "rank_rankl0") / 10
rho3 <- ini_val(q, "frho_tgf_rob") * tgf0
emax3 <- ini_val(q, "emax_tgf_rob")
rho1 <- ini_val(q, "frho_tgf_oc") * tgf0
emax1 <- ini_val(q, "emax_tgf_oc")
a2 <- ini_val(q, "a_cmx_oc")
rho2 <- ini_val(q, "rho_cmx_oc")
g2 <- ini_val(q, "gam_cmx_oc")
derived <- data.frame(
  quantity = c("rho3", "a3", "delta3", "rho1", "a1", "delta1", "delta2", "k_OC->TGF"),
  table1 = c(0.202, 4.18, 34.0, 0.200, 2.18, 16.2, 0.000013, 5.66),
  packaged = c(
    rho3, rho3 + emax3, emax3 * tgf0 / (tgf0 - rho3) - tgf0,
    rho1, rho1 + emax1, emax1 * tgf0 / (tgf0 - rho1) - tgf0,
    ((a2 - rho2) * (pil0^g2 / (a2 - 1)) - pil0^g2)^(1 / g2),
    exp(ini_val(q, "ld_tgf")) * tgf0 / oc0
  )
)
derived$rel_diff_pct <- round(100 * (derived$packaged / derived$table1 - 1), 2)
knitr::kable(derived, digits = 6)
# Every derived constant matches its rounded Table 1 entry to within rounding,
# except a1 (see Assumptions and deviations).
stopifnot(abs(derived$rel_diff_pct[derived$quantity != "a1"]) < 2.5)
```

# Simulation

The trial design is denosumab every 6 months (4320 h) subcutaneously. Each arm
is simulated as one typical subject on a 0-48-month grid.

```{r simulate}
h_per_month <- 720
doses_mg <- c(14, 60, 100, 210)
make_events <- function(dose_mg, id, n_doses = 8, end_month = 48) {
  obs <- data.frame(
    id = id, time = seq(0, end_month, by = 0.25) * h_per_month, amt = 0, evid = 0,
    cmt = "BMD_LS"
  )
  if (dose_mg > 0) {
    dose <- data.frame(
      id = id, time = (seq_len(n_doses) - 1) * 6 * h_per_month, amt = dose_mg * 1000,
      evid = 1, cmt = "depot"
    )
    obs <- rbind(dose, obs)
  }
  obs[order(obs$id, obs$time, -obs$evid), ]
}
ev <- do.call(rbind, Map(make_events, doses_mg, seq_along(doses_mg)))
arm_key <- data.frame(id = seq_along(doses_mg), dose = paste(doses_mg, "mg"))

solve_bmd <- function(ui, events, key) {
  ev_direct <- events
  if (!"BMD_LS" %in% rxode2::rxModelVars(ui)$state) {
    ev_direct$cmt[ev_direct$evid == 0] <- "central"
  }
  out <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(ui, ev_direct, returnType = "data.frame"))
  if (is.null(out$id)) out$id <- 1L
  dplyr::left_join(out, key, by = "id") |>
    dplyr::mutate(month = time / h_per_month)
}
sims <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(names(uis), function(m) {
  solve_bmd(uis[[m]], ev, arm_key) |>
    dplyr::select(id, dose, month, Cc, bmd_pcfb) |>
    dplyr::mutate(model = m)
}))
```

## Denosumab PK

```{r pk-plot}
pk <- dplyr::filter(sims, model == "qsp", month <= 12)
ggplot(pk, aes(month, Cc, colour = dose)) +
  geom_line() +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(
    x = "Time (months)", y = "Free serum denosumab (ng/mL)", colour = "Dose",
    title = "Free denosumab, every-6-month dosing"
  ) +
  theme_bw()
```

## Replicate Figure 5a: fits to months 0-12

```{r data}
# Table S2 of Hasegawa 2018 (digitized by the authors); percent change from
# baseline in lumbar spine BMD.
obs <- data.frame(
  month = c(0, 1, 3, 6, 12, 18, 24, 36, 48),
  `14 mg` = c(0, 1.66, 2.03, 0.906, 2.31, 2.5, 2.5, 7.09, 10.2),
  `60 mg` = c(0, 2.51, 2.98, 4.21, 5.72, 6.3, 7.53, 8.21, 9.37),
  `100 mg` = c(0, 1.32, 3.21, 4.15, 6.13, 6.13, 5.75, 11.4, 12.6),
  `210 mg` = c(0, 1.36, 2.41, 4.21, 4.59, 6.58, 6.58, 0.601, 3.26),
  check.names = FALSE
) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(-month, names_to = "dose", values_to = "bmd_pcfb")
```

```{r fig5a, fig.height = 6}
model_labels <- c(qsp = "Reduced QSP", direct = "Direct response", turnover = "Turnover")
ggplot(dplyr::filter(sims, month <= 12), aes(month, bmd_pcfb)) +
  geom_line(aes(colour = model_labels[model], linetype = model_labels[model])) +
  geom_point(data = dplyr::filter(obs, month <= 12), shape = 1, size = 2) +
  facet_wrap(~ factor(dose, levels = paste(doses_mg, "mg"))) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(-5, 15)) +
  labs(
    x = "Time (months)", y = "BMD % change from baseline", colour = NULL, linetype = NULL,
    title = "Replicates Figure 5a of Hasegawa 2018"
  ) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

## Replicate Figure 5b: extrapolation of the 60 mg arm to 48 months

After month 24 the 14 mg and 100 mg arms were switched to 60 mg and the 210 mg
arm stopped treatment, so, as in the paper, only the 60 mg arm is extrapolated.

```{r fig5b}
ggplot(dplyr::filter(sims, dose == "60 mg"), aes(month, bmd_pcfb)) +
  geom_line(aes(colour = model_labels[model], linetype = model_labels[model])) +
  geom_point(data = dplyr::filter(obs, dose == "60 mg"), shape = 1, size = 2) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 12, linetype = "dotted") +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(-5, 15)) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 48, 12)) +
  labs(
    x = "Time (months)", y = "BMD % change from baseline", colour = NULL, linetype = NULL,
    title = "Replicates Figure 5b of Hasegawa 2018"
  ) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

## Comparison against the published curves

Figure 5 draws each model's prediction as straight segments between the visit
months, so the published values at those months can be read off the figure.
The maintainers read them from the article's Figure 5 to about 0.2 percentage
points. All three models are deterministic typical-value models, so the packaged
predictions are compared to those readings directly.

```{r fig5-compare}
fig5 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~model, ~dose, ~month, ~published,
  "qsp", "60 mg", 1, 1.4,
  "qsp", "60 mg", 3, 3.0,
  "qsp", "60 mg", 6, 3.8,
  "qsp", "60 mg", 12, 4.9,
  "qsp", "60 mg", 24, 6.3,
  "qsp", "60 mg", 36, 7.5,
  "qsp", "60 mg", 48, 8.45,
  "qsp", "14 mg", 3, 2.7,
  "qsp", "14 mg", 6, 1.8,
  "qsp", "14 mg", 12, 2.5,
  "qsp", "100 mg", 12, 5.4,
  "qsp", "210 mg", 12, 5.5,
  "direct", "60 mg", 12, 5.3,
  "direct", "60 mg", 48, 5.7,
  "direct", "14 mg", 6, 1.5,
  "direct", "14 mg", 12, 1.9,
  "turnover", "60 mg", 12, 4.9,
  "turnover", "60 mg", 48, 5.2,
  "turnover", "14 mg", 12, 2.5
)
cmp <- dplyr::inner_join(fig5, sims, by = c("model", "dose", "month")) |>
  dplyr::mutate(simulated = round(bmd_pcfb, 2), diff = round(simulated - published, 2)) |>
  dplyr::select(model, dose, month, published, simulated, diff)
knitr::kable(cmp)
stopifnot(
  nrow(cmp) == nrow(fig5),
  # A transcription error in a rate constant, a dose unit or the PK binding
  # constant moves these curves by whole percentage points; figure-reading
  # error is a few tenths.
  max(abs(cmp$diff)) < 0.5
)
```

The extrapolation result of the paper is reproduced: from month 12 to month 48
the reduced model continues to gain BMD (about 3.6 percentage points), while
both empirical models plateau (gains below 0.5 percentage points).

```{r extrapolation-check}
gain <- sims |>
  dplyr::filter(dose == "60 mg", month %in% c(12, 48)) |>
  dplyr::select(model, month, bmd_pcfb) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = month, values_from = bmd_pcfb, names_prefix = "m") |>
  dplyr::mutate(gain_12_to_48 = m48 - m12)
knitr::kable(gain, digits = 2)
stopifnot(
  gain$gain_12_to_48[gain$model == "qsp"] > 3,
  all(gain$gain_12_to_48[gain$model != "qsp"] < 1)
)
```

## Fit to the training data

```{r training-fit}
train <- dplyr::inner_join(
  dplyr::filter(obs, month > 0, month <= 12),
  dplyr::select(sims, model, dose, month, pred = bmd_pcfb),
  by = c("dose", "month")
) |>
  dplyr::group_by(model) |>
  dplyr::summarise(rmse = sqrt(mean((bmd_pcfb - pred)^2)), .groups = "drop")
knitr::kable(train, digits = 2)
```

All three root-mean-square errors are of the size of the residual standard
deviations the paper estimated (0.62, 0.57 and 0.62 percentage points).

## Untreated reduced model

The reduced model does not start at a steady state. Its baseline-derived
constants were computed from the original model's state at `t0`, but four
parameters were then re-estimated, and the estimated osteoclast degradation rate
(0.0898 /h, against 0.0292 /h before estimation) drives the osteoclast pool
toward a lower level from time zero. Without denosumab the reduced model
therefore predicts a slow BMD gain.

```{r placebo}
pbo <- solve_bmd(uis$qsp, make_events(0, 1), data.frame(id = 1L, dose = "0 mg"))
pbo_tab <- dplyr::filter(pbo, month %in% c(3, 12, 24, 48)) |>
  dplyr::transmute(month, bmd_pcfb = round(bmd_pcfb, 2), oc_relative_to_t0 = round(oc / 0.0012, 3))
knitr::kable(pbo_tab)
```

This drift is a property of the published model, not of the packaging. In the
denosumab arms it is part of the fitted trajectory, so the model should be used
for drug-treated scenarios relative to its own untreated prediction, or as
published, rather than as a model of untreated BMD.

# PKNCA of the shared denosumab PK

The paper reports no NCA of denosumab; the shared PK model is the published
Sutjandra (2011) model with fixed parameters. NCA of the first dosing interval
is provided for orientation. Tmax is resolved only to the 0.25-month (180 h)
simulation grid.

```{r pknca}
nca_dat <- dplyr::filter(sims, model == "qsp", month <= 6) |>
  dplyr::mutate(time = month * h_per_month, treatment = dose) |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  dplyr::distinct(id, time, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, Cc, treatment)
nca_dose <- data.frame(
  id = seq_along(doses_mg), time = 0, amt = doses_mg * 1000,
  treatment = paste(doses_mg, "mg")
)
conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(nca_dat, Cc ~ time | treatment + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(nca_dose, amt ~ time | treatment + id)
intervals <- data.frame(start = 0, end = 6 * h_per_month, cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE, auclast = TRUE)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))
nca_tab <- as.data.frame(nca_res) |>
  dplyr::select(treatment, PPTESTCD, PPORRES) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = PPORRES) |>
  dplyr::arrange(as.numeric(sub(" mg", "", treatment))) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Dose" = treatment, "Cmax free (ng/mL)" = cmax, "Tmax (h)" = tmax,
    "AUC0-6 months free (ng*h/mL)" = auclast
  )
knitr::kable(nca_tab, digits = 1)
cmax <- as.data.frame(nca_res) |> dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD == "cmax")
# Free exposure rises more than dose-proportionally (target-mediated
# disposition): the 210 mg Cmax exceeds 15 times the 14 mg Cmax.
stopifnot(cmax$PPORRES[cmax$treatment == "210 mg"] > 15 * cmax$PPORRES[cmax$treatment == "14 mg"])
```

# Assumptions and deviations

* **PK binding constant, baseline RANKL and RANKL degradation.** The NONMEM
  stream reads these three PK constants from data columns (`KSSINI`, `R00`,
  `KDEG`) that were not published. The authors' MATLAB code for the same
  analysis sets `Kss = 138*10` (1380 ng/mL), `R0 = 614` ng/mL and
  `kdeg = 0.00148` /h, whereas Table 1 lists `K_SS = 138` ng/mL (the
  pre-estimation value of the bone-model `K_SS`, a separate parameter). The
  maintainers settled the PK value with the paper's own Figure 5: the published
  direct-response curve at 14 mg implies a free denosumab trough of about
  1.1 ng/mL at months 6 and 12 (from `5.92 x (1 - exp(-k t)) x C / (2.05 + C)` equal to the
  plotted 1.5 and 1.9), and the PK model gives 1.08 and 1.11 ng/mL with
  `Kss = 1380` ng/mL but about 3e-5 ng/mL with 138 ng/mL. The 1380 ng/mL value,
  with `R0` and `kdeg` as in the MATLAB code, is used for all three models.
* **TGF-beta Hill constant a1.** Table 1 prints a1 = 2.18; the
  stream derives a1 = rho1 + 2 = 2.20. The stream (as run) is followed; the
  difference is 1%.
* **Unprinted BMD exponents.** The powers of the osteoblast and osteoclast
  ratios in Eq 4 (0.0739 and 0.0779) are not in the paper; they are taken from
  the stream, where they are fixed.
* **Body weight.** The stream evaluates the Sutjandra allometric term on ka at
  a fixed 66 kg; the packaged models do the same and have no covariates.
* **Time unit.** The NONMEM fits used a 30-day month. The packaged models are in
  hours; dosing every 6 months is every 4320 h, and the empirical T1/2 of
  3.12 months is 2246.4 h.
* **Residual error.** The paper reports variances; `addSd` is their square root.
  The fitted output was the percent change from baseline (`bmd_pcfb`), which is
  `BMD_LS - 100`; an additive error on either is the same.
* **Positive-reference model not packaged.** The paper also refitted the
  semi-mechanistic bone cycle model of Zheng et al. (2015) as a positive
  reference (Table S1). Its equations in the supplement use a symbol (`PL`) that
  is not defined there, and its initial bone-cycle-unit amounts, which set the
  scale of the off-treatment term, are given only in Zheng 2015. That model is
  not included here.
* **Untreated drift.** See the untreated reduced model section above.
